meaning: A trick that pressures you to buy a gift card and give away its number or PIN as payment.
clues: It pressures you to pay or send money quickly because of a made-up problem.
You are told to buy a store card and read its number and PIN, not wire money or use a check.
The caller may name a utility or office.
A real business or government office will not demand payment this way.
Its name starts with G and has three words.
assumes: A wire transfer sends money through a transfer service
A payment app scam asks you to send money through a payment app
A fake check scam uses a check that later turns out to be fake

decoys.meaning: A trick that gets you to send money by wire transfer, often to a stranger.
A trick that gets you to send money through a payment app.
A trick that uses a check that later turns out to be fake.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Try it with someone you trust. If a caller wants a gift card, hang up and tell a trusted person before you pay.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: A gift card was a gift for a person you knew. It was never a bill payment.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: If you shared the card number, keep the card and receipt. Call the card company right away and report it at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

sources.name: FTC, Avoiding and reporting gift card scams
FTC, Check-out line gift card advice

why: A real business or government office will not demand payment this way.

situations.text: You buy a gift card for your niece and give it to her for her birthday.
situations.why: A gift card is a gift for someone you know, never a bill payment.
